---
title: "ATAC from a common peak matrix"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## Scope and resources

This external-data recipe starts with measured counts over one common peak
universe. It does not require fragments, peak calling, or recount. Website
rendering displays the recipe without downloading data or executing its external
analysis. Run the blocks in a prepared R session with the listed resources.

The source is the [10x PBMC ATAC v2 dataset used by Signac](https://stuartlab.org/signac/articles/pbmc_vignette.html).
Use a new data directory and explicitly download the filtered peak matrix and
the reference sequence. Analysis functions do not download these resources.

```{r prepare-resources}
data_dir <- "atac_data"
dir.create(data_dir)
base <- paste0("https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/2.1.0/",
  "10k_pbmc_ATACv2_nextgem_Chromium_Controller/")
prefix <- "10k_pbmc_ATACv2_nextgem_Chromium_Controller_"
matrix_file <- file.path(data_dir, paste0(prefix, "filtered_peak_bc_matrix.h5"))
utils::download.file(paste0(base, basename(matrix_file)), matrix_file, mode = "wb")
fasta_gz <- file.path(data_dir, "hg38-chr1.fa.gz")
utils::download.file(
  "https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/hg38/chromosomes/chr1.fa.gz",
  fasta_gz, mode = "wb")
fasta <- file.path(data_dir, "hg38-chr1.fa")
Biostrings::writeXStringSet(Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(fasta_gz), fasta)
Rsamtools::indexFa(fasta)
reference <- Rsamtools::FaFile(fasta)
tools::md5sum(c(matrix_file, fasta_gz))
```

The worked acceptance run used R 4.5.2, Seurat 5.3.0, SeuratObject 5.2.0,
Signac 1.16.0, motifmatchr 1.32.0 and chromVAR 1.32.0. These are a tested
combination, not a promise about every historical or development release.
Prepare hdf5r, sequence packages, TFBSTools and JASPAR2020 separately.

## Import and declare the analysis scope

The full source matrix has 165,434 peaks and 10,246 cells. This teaching run
explicitly selects 1,000 cells and chr1, then removes peaks with zero total
counts in those cells. This gives 15,856 peaks. It is a chromosome-scoped
software acceptance run, not a whole-genome PBMC atlas.

```{r import}
atac <- scop::ReadATACData(matrix_file, genome = "hg38", sample = "PBMC_capture")
cells <- withr::with_seed(20261015, sort(sample(colnames(atac), 1000)))
peaks <- rownames(atac)[as.character(GenomicRanges::seqnames(Signac::granges(atac))) == "chr1"]
atac <- subset(atac, cells = cells, features = peaks)
counts <- SeuratObject::LayerData(atac, layer = "counts")
atac <- subset(atac, features = rownames(counts)[Matrix::rowSums(counts) > 0])
atac$capture <- "PBMC_capture"
saveRDS(atac, file.path(data_dir, "atac_counts.rds"))
```

The H5 importer treats its interval labels as 0-based half-open input and stores
1-based closed GRanges. It records original feature/barcode identifiers. Missing
fragments do not invalidate this matrix path. Different sample-specific peak
matrices must first be recounted over common ranges; padding unmeasured peaks
with zeros is not a substitute.

## TF-IDF, LSI and explicit dimensions

TF-IDF weights counts by within-cell frequency and across-cell rarity. Signac
performs this transformation and SVD. SCOP organizes selected features, neighbors,
clusters and UMAP. The selected dimensions are explicit here; the first component
is not automatically evidence of biology or automatically evidence of noise.

```{r representation}
atac <- scop::RunStandardWorkflow(atac,
  assay = "peaks", prefix = "ATACInitial", normalization_method = "TFIDF",
  nHVF = 5000, linear_reduction_dims = 25,
  linear_reduction_dims_use = 2:20, cores = 1)
representation <- SeuratObject::Misc(atac[["ATACInitiallsi"]], "scop_atac_representation")
representation$dimensions
representation$depth_correlation
Seurat::DimPlot(atac, reduction = "ATACInitialUMAP2D", group.by = "ATACInitiallsiclusters")
```

The receipt retains actual cells/features, selected dimensions and Pearson
correlations with raw library depth. Inspect these correlations before selecting
dimensions for a new dataset. Undefined correlations remain NA. A requested ATAC
clustering or UMAP failure terminates the workflow instead of reporting success.

## Sequence motifs and chromVAR

Motif incidence records sequence matches in peaks. Its inputs are ranges,
reference DNA and PWMs; counts are needed later for chromVAR's accessibility
deviations. This small panel demonstrates the data flow rather than a complete
TF screen. Keep stable motif IDs even when display names repeat.

```{r motifs-and-chromvar}
pfm <- TFBSTools::getMatrixSet(JASPAR2020::JASPAR2020, opts = list(
  ID = c("MA0139.1", "MA0080.5", "MA0105.4", "MA0107.1", "MA0039.4", "MA0466.2", "MA0098.3")))
atac <- scop::AddATACMotifs(atac, reference, pfm, genome.id = "hg38")
atac <- scop::RunChromVAR(atac, reference, genome.id = "hg38",
  niterations = 25, seed = 19)
scores <- SeuratObject::LayerData(atac, assay = "chromvar", layer = "data")
receipt <- SeuratObject::Misc(atac[["chromvar"]], "scop_chromvar")
dim(scores)
receipt$background_source
receipt$nonfinite_scores
```

SCOP calls official chromVAR computation and retains native deviations, Z-scores
and actual background indices. Z-scores are stored in `data`, not raw counts.
They describe motif-associated accessibility, not TF expression, binding or
causality. Supplied reference labels document provenance; matching labels alone
do not verify the DNA sequence itself.

## Save and resume

For a regular R checkpoint, `saveRDS(atac, "atac.rds")` and
`readRDS("atac.rds")` preserve the complete object. No dedicated export step
is needed to continue an analysis. The optional interchange example below
adds BED/count files and an external-resource inventory.

```{r export}
scop::ExportATACResults(atac, outdir = "pbmc_matrix_export", assay = "peaks", counts = TRUE)
# In a fresh R session with the same dependencies:
restored <- readRDS("pbmc_matrix_export/object.rds")
SeuratObject::Embeddings(restored[["ATACInitiallsi"]])[1:3, 1:3]
```

The export includes the complete RDS object, selected-assay matrix companions,
metadata, reference intervals, external-resource inventory and file checksums.
RDS preserves R classes; CSV does not preserve all R column classes. Existing
destinations are rejected. Continue with the [fragment workflow](atac-fragments-workflow.html)
only when indexed fragments are actually available.
